overview: This concurrent resolution, passed by both the House and Senate, lets Congress use Emancipation Hall, the large main hall of the Capitol Visitor Center, on June 26, 2025, for a ceremony presenting the Congressional Gold Medal to U.S. Army Rangers who served in World War II. The medal itself was awarded by an earlier law. The Architect of the Capitol, the office that manages the Capitol buildings, sets the conditions for preparing the space. Congress gave it final approval on May 8, 2025.
for: Supporters say it provides a fitting venue to honor World War II Army Rangers with Congress's highest civilian award.
against: Critics say it is a routine ceremonial measure that does not change any law or spending.
